316372.title: Successor conjecture for maximal projective-degree partitions
316372.statement:
For each $n$, let $\lambda^{(n)}_{g\max}\models n$ be a partition of $n$ maximizing its projective degree $g^\lambda$. For a partition $\mu\models n$, define its set of $1$-successors by

$$
N(\mu,1)=\{\lambda\models n+1\mid |\lambda_i-\mu_i|\leq 1\text{ for }1\leq i\leq s\},
$$

where $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s)$. **Successor conjecture.** For all $n$, the maximal projective-degree partition at size $n+1$ satisfies

$$
\lambda^{(n+1)}_{g\max}\in N(\lambda^{(n)}_{g\max},1).
$$

The claim extrapolates an observation verified computationally for $1\leq n<100$; when a maximum is not unique, the source specifies that every maximizer at size $n+1$ should be a $1$-successor of every maximizer at size $n$.
316372.source_name: Dan Bernstein, “Strict Partitions of Maximal Projective Degree”, arXiv:0705.4015 (2007).
316372.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4015

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2007).

319275.title: Tight upper-bound conjecture for admissible vertex counts of normal surfaces
319275.statement:
Let $n$ be the number of tetrahedra in a triangulation, and let $\sigma$ denote its admissible vertex count. For positive $n\neq 1,2,3,5$, equation~ gives the proposed upper bound.

**Tight upper-bound conjecture.** For every positive $n\neq 1,2,3,5$, equation~ gives a tight upper bound on the admissible vertex count $\sigma$. Consequently,

$$
\sigma\in O(17^{n/4}).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the census, in which the pathological triangulations give the maximum observed admissible vertex counts wherever they are defined. It predicts the observed maximum growth rate, but the supplied text gives no resolution beyond these computational observations.
319275.source_name: Benjamin A. Burton, “The complexity of the normal surface solution space”, arXiv:0911.5498 (2010).
319275.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.5498

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2009).

327582.title: All-order upper-bound conjecture for complete arcs
327582.statement:
Let $t_{2}(2,q)$ be the smallest size of a complete arc in $\mathrm{PG}(2,q)$, and let the bounds denoted in the source by 
$$
through
$$
 be the explicit upper bounds obtained from the computed complete arcs and lexiarcs. **All-order upper-bound conjecture.** These bounds hold for every prime power $q\geq109$.
The bounds are proved computationally for all prime powers through $301813$, with additional sporadic computations up to $430007$; the conjecture extrapolates their validity to all prime powers $q\geq109$.
327582.source_name: Daniele Bartoli, Alexander A. Davydov, Giorgio Faina, Alexey A. Kreshchuk, Stefano Marcugini and Fernanda Pambianco, “Tables, bounds and graphics of sizes of complete arcs in the plane PG(2,q) for all q321007 and sporadic q in [323761430007] obtained by an algorithm with fixed order of points (FOP)”, arXiv:1404.0469 (2018).
327582.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0469

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2014).

332225.title: RRP codes exceed the LMRD bound outside the exceptional packet lengths
332225.statement:
Let $v$ be a packet length, and let the **RRP** denote the construction problem referred to in the source. The **LMRD code bound** is the benchmark bound for lifted maximum-rank-distance codes; the echelon-Ferrers construction and its variants are competing constructions.

**RRP bound conjecture.** For any packet length $v\geq 7$ with $v\notin\{8,10\}$, the largest subspace codes that can be obtained by solving the RRP exceed the LMRD code bound and thus are better than the codes resulting from the echelon-Ferrers construction and its variants.

The claim is motivated by computational results for packet lengths through $15$, but the supplied text does not establish it for every stated $v$ and gives no resolution beyond those computations.
332225.source_name: Jingmei Ai, Thomas Honold and Haiteng Liu, “The Expurgation-Augmentation Method for Constructing Good Plane Subspace Codes”, arXiv:1601.01502 (2016).
332225.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.01502

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

332626.title: Conjecture on the maximum length of rich square-free words
332626.statement:
Let $r(n)$ be the maximum length of a rich square-free word over an alphabet of size $n$, and let $w_n$ be the recursively constructed rich square-free word over an alphabet of size $n$. **Conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
r(n)=\operatorname{max}\\{|w_n|,2\cdot|w_{n-1}|+1\\}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the maximum length is the larger of the length of the paper's recursively constructed word and the length obtained from the basic recursion. The computed values for $n=7,8,9,10$ motivate the conjecture, but the exact values for $n=8$ and $n=9$ were not computable in the paper.
332626.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01058

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

333945.title: The path conjecture for maximum von Neumann entropy of trees
333945.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices. Define its scaled Laplacian by $\rho(T):=L(T)/\operatorname{tr}L(T)$, where $L(T)$ is the combinatorial Laplacian. The von Neumann entropy $S(T)$ is the Shannon entropy of the eigenvalues of $\rho(T)$.

**The path conjecture.** For all trees on $n$ vertices, the maximum von Neumann entropy is attained by the path $P_n$.

The source reports computational verification for trees up to $15$ vertices. It does not establish the conjecture in general.
333945.source_name: Michael Dairyko, Leslie Hogben, Jephian C. -H. Lin, Joshua Lockhart, David Roberson, Simone Severini and Michael Young, “Note on von Neumann and Rényi entropies of a Graph”, arXiv:1609.00420 (2016).
333945.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00420

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

334107.title: Universality classes for centrally weighted small-step models
334107.statement: Let ${\mathcal{S}}$ be one of the 19 small-step lattice-path models with finite non-zero orbit sum, and consider its centrally weighted walk model. Let $Q(1,1;t)$ be the corresponding generating function, and let the universality classes be the classes determined by the minimum of the inventory on the quarter-plane cone. **Garbit, Mustapha and Raschel's universality-class conjecture.** The divisions into universality classes for centrally weighted walk models are given by the Garbit–Mustapha–Raschel conjecture. The source states that this is verified for GB walks with central weighting, but does not establish it for all 19 models.
334107.source_name: Julien Courtiel, Stephen Melczer, Marni Mishna and Kilian Raschel, “Weighted Lattice Walks and Universality Classes”, arXiv:1609.05839 (2017).
334107.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05839

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

335186.title: Asymptotic conjecture that the normalized constants $\alpha_r$ vanish
335186.statement:
For fixed $r\geq 1$, let $\alpha_r$ be the smallest real number such that

$$
f_r(n)\leq \alpha_r(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor r/2\rfloor}.
$$

Here $f_r(n)$ is the minimum number of complete $r$-partite $r$-graphs needed to decompose the complete $r$-graph on $n$ vertices.

**Vanishing-$\alpha_r$ conjecture.** We have

$$
\alpha_r\rightarrow 0\quad\text{as }r\rightarrow\infty.
$$

The initial construction gives $\alpha_r\leq 1$ for all $r$, while the paper establishes $\alpha_r\leq \frac{14}{15}$ for even $r$. The conjecture predicts a substantially stronger improvement as the uniformity grows.
335186.source_name: Imre Leader, Luka Milićević and Ta Sheng Tan, “Decomposing the Complete r-Graph”, arXiv:1701.08335 (2017).
335186.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.08335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

335370.title: Hypohamiltonian oddness-resistance conjecture
335370.statement:
A **hypohamiltonian** graph is a non-Hamiltonian graph $G$ such that $G-v$ is Hamiltonian for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. Let $\mu_3(G)$ be the minimum number of edges missed by a list of three 1-factors of $G$.

**Hypohamiltonian oddness-resistance conjecture.** If $G$ is a cubic class 2 graph and $G$ is hypohamiltonian, then

$$
\mu_3(G)=3.
$$

If true, this would imply that hypohamiltonian snarks have excessive index $5$, hence satisfy Berge's conjecture. The assertion was verified for all hypohamiltonian class 2 graphs with at most 36 vertices, but remains open generally.
335370.source_name: M. A. Fiol, G. Mazzuoccolo and E. Steffen, “On measures of edge-uncolorability of cubic graphs: A brief survey and some new results”, arXiv:1702.07156 (2017).
335370.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07156

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

335503.title: Recursive width conjecture for torus knots
335503.statement:
Let $T_{p,q}$ denote the torus knot associated to positive coprime integers $p$ and $q$, and let $\widehat{HFK}(T_{p,q})$ be its knot Floer homology. Write $\operatorname{width}\widehat{HFK}(T_{p,q})$ for its width. **Recursive width conjecture.** If $p<q$, then

$$
\operatorname{width}\widehat{HFK}(T_{p,q})-\operatorname{width}\widehat{HFK}(T_{p,q-p})=\left\lfloor\frac{(p-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

Together with the base case $\operatorname{width}\widehat{HFK}(T_{1,q})=1$ and the symmetry $T_{p,q}=T_{q,p}$, this would recursively determine the width for every torus knot. The conjecture is known for $q\equiv\pm1\pmod p$ and for $p\leq6$, and computer computations verify it for $p,q<250$; its general validity remains open.
335503.source_name: Kaitian Jin, Adam M. Lowrance, Eli Polston and Yanjie Zheng, “On the Turaev genus of torus knots”, arXiv:1703.02506 (2017).
335503.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02506

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

336500.title: Kellner's large-prime-factor conjecture for Bernoulli-polynomial denominators
336500.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $s_p(n)$ denote the sum of the base-$p$ digits of $n$, and define

$$
\mathfrak P_n=\prod_{p\text{ prime}:\,s_p(n)\ge p}p.
$$

Let $P(m)$ be the largest prime factor of $m$. **Kellner's conjecture.** For $n>192$,

$$
P(\mathfrak P_n)>\sqrt n.
$$

Equivalently, using $\mathfrak P_n^+=\prod_{p>\sqrt n,\,s_p(n)\ge p}p$, one has $\mathfrak P_n^+>1$ for every $n>192$. The source states that this is established, apart from the numerical threshold $192$, in a stronger form in its Theorem 2.
336500.source_name: Olivier Bordellès, Florian Luca, Pieter Moree and Igor E. Shparlinski, “Denominators of Bernoulli polynomials”, arXiv:1706.09804 (2017).
336500.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09804

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

337334.title: 321-avoidance conjecture for shortest universal permutations
337334.statement:
A permutation $\pi$ is **$n$-universal for the class of $321$-avoiding permutations** if it contains every $321$-avoiding permutation of length $n$. A shortest such permutation is one of minimum possible length among permutations with this property.

**321-avoidance conjecture.** For every $n$, at least one shortest permutation that is $n$-universal for the class of $321$-avoiding permutations avoids $321$ itself.

The analogous property is proved in the paper for layered permutations, whereas computational evidence suggests it for the class of $321$-avoiding permutations. Its general validity remains open.
337334.source_name: Michael Albert, Michael Engen, Jay Pantone and Vincent Vatter, “Universal layered permutations”, arXiv:1710.04240 (2017).
337334.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.04240

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

337993.title: Lexi-bounds conjecture for short linear codes and saturating sets
337993.statement:
Let $\ell_q(r,3)$ be the length function, let $\ell_q(r,3,5)$ be the $d$-length function, let $s_q(r-1,2)$ be the smallest size of a $2$-saturating set in $\mathrm{PG}(r-1,q)$, and let $s_q^{\operatorname{arc}}(3)$ be the smallest size of a complete arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. **Lexi-bounds conjecture.** The following upper bounds hold:

$$
\ell_q(4,3)=s_q(3,2)\leq\ell_q(4,3,5)=s_q^{\operatorname{arc}}(3)<2.8\sqrt[3]{\ln q}\,\sqrt[3]{q}
$$

for all $q\geq 11$, and

$$
\ell_q(5,3)=s_q(4,2)\leq\ell_q(5,3,5)<3\sqrt[3]{\ln q}\,\sqrt[3]{q^2}
$$

for all $q\geq 5$. These bounds improve earlier constants and connect short linear codes with saturating sets and complete arcs; the source presents them as conjectural bounds based on computational observations.
337993.source_name: Daniele Bartoli, Alexander A. Davydov, Stefano Marcugini and Fernanda Pambianco, “Tables, bounds and graphics of short linear codes with covering radius 3 and codimension 4 and 5”, arXiv:1712.07078 (2020).
337993.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07078

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

339312.title: The exact 3- and 4-connectivity conjecture for balanced hypercubes
339312.statement:
Let $BH_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional balanced hypercube, and let $\kappa^h(BH_n)$ denote its $h$-connectivity. The paper establishes the relevant upper bound for $n\geq5$.

**Exact connectivity conjecture.**

$$
\kappa^3(BH_n)=\kappa^4(BH_n)=12n-24\quad\text{for }n\geq5.
$$

This would determine the 3- and 4-connectivity of balanced hypercubes for all dimensions $n\geq5$; the upper bound is known, but its tightness remains open.
339312.source_name: Huazhong Lü and Tingzeng Wu, “The restricted h-connectivity of balanced hypercubes”, arXiv:1805.08461 (2018).
339312.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.08461

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2018). “As the upper bound we obtained above is tight for $n=3$, we post the following conjecture as an open problem.”

339395.title: Minimal polynomial conjecture for orientation-reversing stretch factors on odd-genus orientable surfaces
339395.statement:
Let $S_g$ be the closed orientable surface of genus $g$, and let $\delta^+_{\mathrm{rev}}(S_g)$ be the minimal stretch factor among orientation-reversing pseudo-Anosov homeomorphisms of $S_g$ with orientable invariant foliations. For a real number $r>1$, call it the largest root of a polynomial if it is the greatest real root of that polynomial.

**Odd-genus orientation-reversing stretch factor conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, $\delta^+_{\mathrm{rev}}(S_{2k-1})$ is the largest root of

$$
x^{4k}-x^{2k+1}-x^{2k-1}-1.
$$

The conjecture follows the computed values for odd genera through $11$ and gives a uniform formula for the odd-genus sequence. The general statement remains open.
339395.source_name: Livio Liechti and Balázs Strenner, “Minimal pseudo-Anosov stretch factors on nonoriented surfaces”, arXiv:1806.00033 (2020).
339395.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.00033

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

339655.title: Upper-bound conjecture for normal form limit values
339655.statement:
For every odd integer $t\geqslant 9$, let $N_t$ be the index

$$
N_t=t+4L_t+3,
$$

where

$$
L_t=\max\left\{\ell\in\mathbb{N}_0:t>u_\ell\right\}=\left\lceil\frac{-t-2+\sqrt{5t^2-4t-12}}{4}\right\rceil-1,
$$

and let $m_t$ be the limit of the normal form orbit and $y_{N_t}$ its term at index $N_t$. The **upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
m_t<y_{N_t}.
$$

The paper has proved lower bounds for $m_t$ and the transit time and reports that available evidence suggests an upper bound by the largest term in the regular phase. The stated inequality remains conjectural here.
339655.source_name: Jonathan Hoseana and Franco Vivaldi, “Geometrical Properties of the Mean-Median Map”, arXiv:1806.10184 (2019).
339655.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.10184

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2018). “In , both conjectures were proved to hold within an explicitly-determined real neighbourhood of $x=\frac{1}{2}$, where $m$ turns out to be affine.”

341603.title: Maximum common-prefix conjecture for uniform squarefree morphisms
341603.statement: Let $T$ be the alphabet, and let an **$n$-uniform squarefree morphism** be a morphism $h:T^*\to T^*$ for which every image $h(a)$ has length $n$ and which maps squarefree words to squarefree words. Let $\operatorname{lcp}(h)$ be the length of the longest common prefix of the images $\{h(a):a\in T\}$, and let $\operatorname{lcp}(n)$ be the maximum value of $\operatorname{lcp}(h)$ over all $n$-uniform squarefree morphisms $h:T^*\to T^*$. **Maximum common-prefix conjecture.** For every $n\geq 30$, there exists an $n$-uniform squarefree morphism $h:T^*\to T^*$ such that $\operatorname{lcp}(h)=n-6$. The computed values for $18\leq n\leq 70$ suggest this conjecture; its validity for all $n\geq 30$ remains open.
341603.source_name: James Currie, Tero Harju, Pascal Ochem and Narad Rampersad, “Some further results on squarefree arithmetic progressions in infinite words”, arXiv:1901.06351 (2019).
341603.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.06351

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

342062.title: Uniqueness conjecture for connected well-indumatched graphs of girth 11
342062.statement: Let $G$ be a connected well-indumatched graph of girth $11$, and let $C_{11}$ denote the cycle on $11$ vertices. **The girth-11 uniqueness conjecture.** The cycle $C_{11}$ is the only connected well-indumatched graph of girth $11$. This would settle the only remaining girth case not covered by the paper's dichotomy: for every other girth at least $3$, the authors either prove nonexistence or construct an infinite family of well-indumatched graphs. The conjecture remains open here; the paper establishes only that $C_{11}$ is the sole minimal well-indumatched graph of girth $11$.
342062.source_name: S. Akbari, T. Ekim, A. H. Ghodrati and S. Zare, “Well-indumatched Trees and Graphs of Bounded Girth”, arXiv:1903.03197 (2019).
342062.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.03197

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

342261.title: Conjecture that the maximum Jacobsthal function eventually exceeds the primorial function
342261.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $h(k)=j(p_k\#)$ be the Jacobsthal function at the product of the first $k$ primes, and let $H(k)$ be the maximum of the Jacobsthal function over products of $k$ distinct primes:

$$
H(k)=\max_{d_{\mathbb{P}}(n)=k}j(n).
$$

**Eventual strict inequality conjecture.** For all $k\ge 33$,

$$
H(k)>h(k).
$$

This conjecture reverses the equality proposed by Jacobsthal and is motivated by the computational results in the paper. The source presents it as one of three new conjectures, with no resolution supplied.
342261.source_name: Mario Ziller, “New computational results on a conjecture of Jacobsthal”, arXiv:1903.11973 (2019).
342261.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.11973

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

342882.title: The c-unbounded lower-bound conjecture for hypergraph Ramsey numbers
342882.statement:
Let $k\geq 10$ be an integer, and let $p$ and $q$ be integers satisfying $p\geq k+2$ and $q\geq k+1$. Write $r_k(p,q)$ for the smallest integer $n$ such that every red-blue coloring of the $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set contains either a red $p$-element set or a blue $q$-element set. **The c-unbounded lower-bound conjecture.** For every such $k$, $p$, and $q$, 

$$
r_k(p,q)\geq (p-1)\bigl(r_k(p-1,q)-1\bigr)+1.
$$

This conjecture extends the lower-bound recurrence proved computationally in the paper, removing the fixed upper bound on the parameter $c$ from the corresponding theorem. It is motivated by the expectation that constructing additional SAT instances for larger values of $k$ would improve the established lower bound.
342882.source_name: S. Cliff Liu, “Lower Bounds for Small Ramsey Numbers on Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1906.00132 (2019).
342882.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.00132

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

342911.title: The eventual extremal conjecture for triangles in $K_4$-saturated graphs
342911.statement:
Let $t$ be an integer with $t\geq 4$. For an $n$-vertex $K_4$-saturated graph, let $\operatorname{sat}_t(n,K_3,K_4)$ denote the minimum number of triangles among graphs with minimum degree $t$, and let $H_t(n)$ be the graph defined in the paper. **Eventual extremal conjecture.** There is an integer $n_t$ such that for every $n\geq n_t$,

$$
\operatorname{sat}_t(n,K_3,K_4)=2n+2t-12
$$

and $H_t(n)$ is the unique extremal graph. The conjecture asserts that the upper bound supplied by $H_t(n)$ is eventually sharp, with no other extremal graphs. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source; the paper proves the corresponding upper bound and establishes related results for minimum degree $4$.
342911.source_name: Benjamin Cole, Albert Curry, David Davini and Craig Timmons, “Triangles in K_s-saturated graphs with minimum degree t”, arXiv:1906.02154 (2019).
342911.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02154

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2019).

343415.title: Gyárfás's extremal conjecture for monochromatic components in Steiner triple systems
343415.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ be the family of Steiner triple systems on $n$ points. For a Steiner triple system $S$, let $\alpha^*_3(S)$ denote the maximum size of a 3-independent set, and let $\mathrm{mc}_3(S)$ denote the minimum, over all 3-edge-colorings of $S$, of the order of a largest monochromatic component. **Gyárfás's conjecture.** For all $n\equiv 1,3 \bmod 6$, 

$$
\max_{S\in \mathcal{S}_n} \alpha^*_3(S)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{3}\right\rfloor-1
$$

and

$$
\min_{S\in \mathcal{S}_n} \mathrm{mc}_3(S)=\left\lceil\frac{2n}{3}\right\rceil+1.
$$

The conjecture is best possible in light of the cited lower and upper bounds, and the second assertion is known when $n\equiv 3\pmod {18}$; the general case remains open.
343415.source_name: Louis DeBiasio and Michael Tait, “Large monochromatic components in 3-edge-colored Steiner triple systems”, arXiv:1908.00837 (2020).
343415.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.00837

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

345406.title: Dimension-five self-orthogonal distance conjecture
345406.statement:
Let $d(n,5)$ denote the largest minimum distance of a binary linear $[n,5]$ code, and let $\dso(n,5)$ denote the largest minimum distance of a binary self-orthogonal $[n,5]$ code. For integers $n\ge 10$ satisfying $n\neq 13$ and $n\equiv_{31}6,13,14,21,22,28,29$, consider optimal self-orthogonal codes of length $n$ and dimension $5$. **Dimension-five self-orthogonal distance conjecture.**

$$
\dso(n,5)=d(n,5)-2.
$$

Equivalently, there are no $[n,5,d(n,5)]$ self-orthogonal codes. The conjecture is based on the tabulated optimal self-orthogonal codes and computations using random codes for the indicated parameter range; the source gives no proof or resolution for all such $n$.
345406.source_name: Jon-Lark Kim, Young-Hun Kim and Nari Lee, “Embedding linear codes into self-orthogonal codes and their optimal minimum distances”, arXiv:2002.01643 (2021).
345406.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01643

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

345669.title: Increasing-pattern extremal conjecture for distant-pattern avoidance
345669.statement:
Let $m\geq3$ and $r\geq1$, and let $q$ be any classical pattern of size $m$. **Increasing-pattern extremal conjecture.** There exists $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every natural number $n>n_0$,

$$
|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(\operatorname{dist}_{r}(12\cdots m))|\geq|\operatorname{Av}_{n}(\operatorname{dist}_{r}(q))|.
$$

Thus, among classical patterns of size $m$, the increasing pattern is conjectured to have asymptotically largest distant-pattern avoidance classes for each fixed gap size $r$. The claim is listed among the paper's open problems and is unresolved in the supplied source.
345669.source_name: Stoyan Dimitrov, “On permutation patterns with constrained gap sizes”, arXiv:2002.12322 (2021).
345669.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12322

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “Section mentions a few unresolved conjectures, namely Conjecture , and , all related to Stanley--Wilf type results.”

346378.title: De Caen–Gregory–Pritikin biclique-cover conjecture for complete graphs
346378.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. For a positive integer $k$, let $\operatorname{bp}_k(K_n)$ denote the minimum size of a collection of bicliques of $K_n$ in which every edge belongs to exactly $k$ bicliques.

**De Caen–Gregory–Pritikin conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$,

$$
\operatorname{bp}_k(K_n)=n-1
$$

for all sufficiently large $n$.

The lower bound $\operatorname{bp}_k(K_n)\geq n-1$ is known for every $k$, and the conjecture is proved for $k\leq 18$ using constructions from design theory. The general case remains open; the best-known upper bound is $O(kn)$.
346378.source_name: Dhruv Rohatgi, John C. Urschel and Jake Wellens, “Regarding two conjectures on clique and biclique partitions”, arXiv:2005.02529 (2020).
346378.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.02529

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2020).

347861.title: Fine torus conjecture for discretizing integral seminorms
347861.statement:
Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a nondegenerate integral convex polytope containing the origin. A fine structure on $\mathbb R^d$ is required to be $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic, and $d_{\widetilde F}$ denotes its induced metric. **Fine torus conjecture.** There exists such a fine structure $\widetilde F$ satisfying

$$
d_{\widetilde F}(x,x+v)=\max_{\varphi\in K}\varphi(v)=:\|v\|_K
$$

for every $v\in\mathbb Z^d$ and every vertex $x$ of $\widetilde F$, with exactly $d!^2|K|$ $d$-dimensional cells up to integer translations. The source presents this as a conjectural optimal discretization of integral seminorms; the discretization problem is noted to be open already in dimension three for the cube, where the conjectured minimum is 36 tetrahedra per period.
347861.source_name: Marcos Cossarini, “Discrete surfaces with length and area and minimal fillings of the circle”, arXiv:2009.02415 (2020).
347861.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02415

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

348207.title: The period dichotomy conjecture for concatenated decimal numbers
348207.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number with $n
e 10$, and let $r(n)$ denote the reversal of the decimal digits of $n$. Let $omega(n)$ be the smallest period and $omega_f(n)$ the constructively obtained possible period associated with $n$. Assume $n
e r(n)$. **Period dichotomy conjecture.** Then

$$
\omega(n)=1\quad\text{or}\quad\omega(n)=\omega_f(n).
$$

The construction proves that $\omega(n)$ divides $\omega_f(n)$, but the table suggests that the smallest period is always either trivial or equal to the constructed period. Whether this dichotomy holds for every admissible $n$ remains open.
348207.source_name: Daniel Tsai, “A recurring pattern in natural numbers of a certain property”, arXiv:2010.03151 (2020).
348207.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03151

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

348788.title: Existence of the asymptotic duplication-distance limit
348788.statement:
For an alphabet with $k$ letters, let $d(W)$ be the minimum number of single square reductions needed to turn a word $W$ into a square-free word, and let $d_k(n)$ be the maximum value of $d(W)$ over words of length $n$. **Limit-existence conjecture.** For every $k\geqslant 2$, the limit

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{d_k(n)}{n}
$$

exists. For $k=2$, this limit is known to exist and is bounded between $0.045$ and $0.4$; existence for larger alphabets, including $k=3$, remains open.
348788.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk and Szymon Stankiewicz, “Square-free reducts of words”, arXiv:2011.12822 (2020).
348788.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.12822

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

348873.title: The folded-hypercube doubly resolving set conjecture
348873.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the folded $n$-cube, and let $\beta(F_n)$ and $\Psi(F_n)$ denote its metric dimension and minimal doubly resolving set number, respectively. **Folded-hypercube conjecture.** For every integer $n\ge 2$,

$$
\beta(F_n)\le \Psi(F_n) \le \beta(F_n)+1.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computations for $n\le 10$ and would determine the gap between the two invariants up to one; its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.
348873.source_name: Changhong Lu and Qingjie Ye, “A bridge between the minimal doubly resolving set problem in (folded) hypercubes and the coin weighing problem”, arXiv:2012.00396 (2021).
348873.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00396

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2020). “Using the result of the coin weighing problem, we prove that $\Psi(Q_n)\le \Psi(Q_{n+1})\le \Psi(Q_n)+1$, which answer an open question in .”

351432.title: The $T$-module normalizer conjecture for finite monomial groups
351432.statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $D_{\{p\}'}$ denote the relevant diagonal module, and let $T$ be a non-solvable transitive subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(p)$. Write $N_{\mathrm{Sym}(p)}(T)$ for the normalizer of $T$ in $\mathrm{Sym}(p)$. **The $T$-module normalizer conjecture.** Every finite $T$-submodule of $D_{\{p\}'}$ is an $N_{\mathrm{Sym}(p)}(T)$-submodule. This conjecture concerns the $T$-module listing problem that obstructs the classification of finite irreducible monomial subgroups; the supplied text gives computational evidence and notes that the smallest degree in which it could fail is $73$, but does not state a resolution.
351432.source_name: Z. Bácskai, D. L. Flannery and E. A. O'Brien, “Classifying finite monomial linear groups of prime degree in characteristic zero”, arXiv:2107.12252 (2021).
351432.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12252

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

351763.title: The $T_{16}(n)$ conjecture for $(5;4)$- and $(5;5)$-extremal graphs
351763.statement: Let $T_{16}(n)$ be the balanced complete $16$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. For a parameter tuple $(k;s)$, an $(k;s)$-extremal graph is an $n$-vertex graph attaining the maximum in the corresponding Erdős–Rothschild problem. **$T_{16}(n)$ extremal graph conjecture.** There exists $n_0>0$ such that for all $n\geq n_0$, $T_{16}(n)$ is the unique $(5;4)$-extremal graph and the unique $(5;5)$-extremal graph. This conjecture is motivated by the uniform solutions identified for the cases $(5;4)$ and $(5;5)$, whose corresponding optimisation solution has $r=16$ and whose colourings arise from $\mathbb{F}_4^2$.
351763.source_name: Oleg Pikhurko and Katherine Staden, “Exact solutions to the Erdős-Rothschild problem”, arXiv:2108.12789 (2023).
351763.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12789

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

352533.title: Spectral cycle-length constant conjecture
352533.statement:
Let $C$ be a positive constant. For every $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<C$ and all sufficiently large $n$, consider every graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying

$$
\lambda(G)>\sqrt{\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor}.
$$

**Spectral cycle-length conjecture.** The largest such constant $C$ is characterized by the property that every such graph contains a cycle of every length $t\le (C-\varepsilon)n$. The source subsequently conjectures that $C=1/2$. This would improve the known bound $C=1/320$; the exact optimal constant remains open.
352533.source_name: Yongtao Li, Weijun Liu and Lihua Feng, “A survey on spectral conditions for some extremal graph problems”, arXiv:2111.03309 (2022).
352533.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.03309

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2021). “The case $k=1$ in Conjecture was early proved by Favaron, Mah\'{e}o and Sacl\'{e} .”

384831.title: Failure of MC
384831.statement:
Show that Monte-Carlo fails on the SBM below the KS bound. This is related to the quantity $Z(\alpha) = \sum_{\tau: \alpha(\sigma,\tau) \approx \alpha} P(G | \tau)$. We want to understand $\mathbb{E}_{G | \sigma} \log Z(\alpha)$. Here $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are colorings of the vertices and $\alpha$ is the overlap matrix

$$
\alpha_{rs} = \frac{|\sigma^{-1}(r) \cap \tau^{-1}(s)|}{n/k}.
$$

It is tractible to compute the annealed average $\mathbb{E}_{G | \sigma} Z(\alpha)$. Is this quantity related?
384831.source_name: AimPL: Connecting communities via the block model (posed by Cris Moore)

386312.title: Problems (problem 4)
386312.statement:
Let $X \sim MVN(\theta, I_d)$, where $I_d$ denotes the $d$-dimensional identity matrix. Consider the problem of estimating $\theta$ using estimators of the form $X + h(X)$, where $h$ is in some class $\mathcal{H}$ of functions. By SURE,

$$
\hat{r}_h = d + 2\nabla \cdot h(X) + \|h(X)\|^2
$$

is an unbiased estimator of the risk associated with $h$. Let

$$
h^* &= \text{arg min} (h \in \mathcal{H}: \hat{r}_h) \\
\hat{\theta}^* &= X + h^*(X).
$$

Find an unbiased estimator $r^{**}$ of the risk $\mathbb{E}(\|\hat{\theta}^* - \theta\|^2)$ of $\hat{\theta}^*$.
386312.source_name: AimPL: Stein's method and applications in high-dimensional statistics (posed by Persi Diaconis)

390045.title: Problem 2.17 — (Nonarithmetic extremal surfaces).
390045.statement: (Nonarithmetic extremal surfaces). Give answers to all of the above problems on automorphisms of Riemann surfaces for the collection of non-arithmetic surfaces. For example find bounds on orders of automorphism groups which are nilpotent, solvable, p-groups, etc. Prove that these bounds are sharp for infinitely many g. Determine the frequency of those g for which such bounds are sharp. Determine the least genus for which the bounds are sharp. The model result for these kind of problems is the following.
390045.source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

396900.title: Formal analysis of locality, sparsity, and local maxima for bounded biharmonic weights
396900.statement: For the bounded biharmonic weights w_j defined as minimizers of the Laplacian energy subject to the handle interpolation, cage-face linearity, partition-of-unity, and bounds in equations (2)\(6) of the report, formally prove or disprove the experimentally observed properties of locality, sparsity, and absence of local maxima. In the report, locality informally means that if a locally shortest shape-aware path from a point to a handle passes near another handle, the first handle's weight should vanish at that point; sparsity means that each point should be influenced by only a few nearby handles; and absence of local maxima means that each weight should attain its global maximum value 1 on its handle and have no other local maxima.
396900.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/07](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4796), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

398710.title: Strict positivity of the Green–Kubo conductivity with positive coupling and noise
398710.statement:
For the chain of Hamiltonian cells perturbed by an energy-preserving noise of intensity $\varsigma>0$ and coupled by a smooth nearest-neighbor potential of strength $\varepsilon$, prove or disprove the conjecture that
\[
\kappa(\varepsilon,\varsigma)>0\qquad\text{whenever }\varepsilon>0\text{ and }\varsigma>0.
\]
Equivalently, under the report’s setup, determine whether there are no stable heat insulators when both the coupling and the noise are positive.
398710.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/52](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12726), page 12. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

398960.title: Narayana numbers in an identity involving semistandard Young tableaux
398960.statement:
For integers $m\ge r\ge l\ge 1$ and $1\le \beta<m$, let $\operatorname{SSYT}_{r,l}(m)$ denote the number of semistandard Young tableaux of shape consisting of two columns of lengths $r\ge l$, with no entry exceeding $m$. Let $Y_{r,l}^{\beta}(m)$ denote the number of such tableaux in which the number $\beta$ appears somewhere in the second column. The identity

$$Y_{r,l}^{\beta}(m)=\sum_{1\le f\le e\le\beta}N_{e-1,f-1}\,\operatorname{SSYT}_{r-f,l-f}(m-e),$$

where

$$N_{e,f}=\frac{1}{e}\binom{e}{f+1}\binom{e}{f},$$

has a recursive proof. Find a proof of the formula that explains the occurrence of the Narayana numbers.
398960.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12872), page 81. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

401592.title: Non-random unitary-matrix examples for a minimum output entropy counterexample
401592.statement:
Can one find a constant $C>0$, an integer $k>\\exp(2C^2)$, and unitary matrices $U_1,\ldots,U_k\in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ such that, for any $n^2$ matrix coefficients $a_{ij}$, 
$$
\left\|\sum_{i\ne j} a_{ij}U_iU_j^*\right\|\le C\sqrt{\sum_{i\ne j}|a_{ij}|^2}
$$
where the norm is the operator norm on the matrices? The requested examples are to be non-random; any such example would give a counterexample to the minimum output entropy additivity conjecture.
401592.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2018/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16163), page 81. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

404292.title: Densities of primes meeting polynomial orbits
404292.statement: Given an arbitrary polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, determine the natural density $\delta_c(f,a,a_0)$ of primes $p$ such that, for the orbit $a_{n+1}=f(a_n)$ with initial value $a_0\in\mathbb{Z}$, one has $a_n\equiv a\pmod p$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$, for a positive proportion of $a\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $a_0\in\mathbb{Z}$.
404292.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2023/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14297740), page 33. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
